sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 12.8% a year from $4.86 billion in FY2016 to $14.3 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F198], but the path was two step changes rather than a smooth climb.
FY2021 was the first: revenue rose 89.1% to $16.1 billion [F6][D241], with REGEN-COV contributing 66.4pp of that growth [D582] and US net product sales 77.1pp [D471].
FY2022 reversed it, revenue falling 24.3% to $12.2 billion [F7][D292] as REGEN-COV dropped to zero [S49] and subtracted 36.3pp [D585].
The second step was the Sanofi profit share: collaboration revenue grew 167.3% in FY2023 [D516] and reached 51.1% of revenue by FY2025 [D521], while net product sales fell 17.3% in FY2025 [D506].

Note that FY2018 and FY2019 revenue in the table is a later recast ($5.15 billion and $6.56 billion) against $6.71 billion and $7.86 billion first reported [F3][X3][F4][X4], so growth spanning those years mixes two presentations.
In FY2025 the growth engine was Regeneron's share of Sanofi antibody profits, up 33.6% and adding 9.3pp of revenue growth [D591][D592], on 36.5% of revenue [D590].
That increase was driven by higher profits primarily associated with an increase in Dupixent sales [P9].
Offsetting it, US EYLEA sales fell 42.4% and subtracted 14.2pp [D577][D578], on lower volumes from competitive pressure and the EYLEA HD transition plus a lower net selling price [P10].
EYLEA HD partly filled the gap, growing 36.3% and adding 3.1pp [D613][D614], on higher volumes partly offset by a lower net selling price [P11].
Operating income fell 10.3% against 1.0% revenue growth [D441][D440], so there was no operating leverage; diluted EPS still grew 8.2% [D444] as the diluted share count fell 5.6% [D459].
Operating margin of 24.9% in FY2025 is the window low, 9.7pp below the 34.6% median and 30.8pp below the FY2021 high of 55.7% [F30][D749][D751][D750].
The latest 3.2pp decline came from R&D adding 4.7pp of cost, partly offset by SG&A giving back 2.0pp [D453][D465][D466].
R&D rose 14.0% to $5.85 billion, or 40.8% of revenue [D455][X34][D420]; the filing describes the program composition but states no single cause for the increase [P6].
SG&A fell 8.6% [D456], primarily due to lower charitable contributions to Good Days [P5].
Net margin held at 31.4% even as operating margin fell [F50], because other income of $1.65 billion [X117] and a 13.9% tax rate [D427] lifted net income 2.1% [D442].
Operating cash flow of $4.98 billion was 1.11x net income and free cash flow of $4.08 billion was 0.91x, against a window median of 0.88x [F80][D428][F100][D429][D763].
Free cash flow margin of 28.4% sits above the 26.4% window median [D425][D757] and in the 86th percentile of seven biopharma peers [D776].
Capex rose 18.9% to $898 million, 6.3% of revenue and 1.65x D&A [D447][F90][D424][D430], reflecting the multi-year build-out the FY2023 filing flagged [P19].
Stock-based compensation of $994 million equalled 20.0% of operating cash flow [X77][D431], so cash conversion leans on a non-cash add-back.
Net cash reached $16.9 billion, 117.7% of revenue [D434][D435], in the 100th percentile of eight biopharma peers against a median of -50.7% [D780][D781].
Debt is a flat $1.99 billion [F187], and the current ratio of 4.13x sits above the 3.97x window median [F180][D766].
Buybacks plus dividends of $3.81 billion consumed 93.3% of free cash flow in FY2025 [D436][D437], including a first $370 million dividend [X140].
That, plus a 5.6% share-count reduction [D459], is why EPS grew faster than net income; return on average equity of 14.9% still ranks in the 25th percentile of eight peers [D439][D784].

Operating margin has fallen four straight years, 30.7pp from the FY2021 peak to the FY2025 window low [R1][F26][F30][D749], and the EYLEA franchise erosion behind it is structural rather than one-off [P10].

The revenue basis break is material: FY2018 and FY2019 in the table are recasts ($5.15 billion and $6.56 billion) versus $6.71 billion and $7.86 billion first reported [R2][F3][X3][F4][X4], so any growth or margin spanning those years mixes presentations.
The FY2021 R&D and FY2020 receivables recasts are small relative to the lines they sit in and do not change any conclusion here [R3][R4].
Operating margin: a print below the FY2025 low of 24.9% [F30][D749] would confirm the four-year slide, while a recovery toward the 34.6% median [D751] would reverse it; the FY2026 10-K will show it.
US EYLEA sales: another decline from the FY2025 $2.75 billion [S43] would extend the 42.4% drop [D577], whereas stabilization would signal the HD transition has found a floor.
R&D as a share of revenue: holding above the FY2025 40.8% [D420] keeps pressure on margin, while a move back toward the 34.6% median [D760] would restore operating leverage.
